transcript: The Public, in trailblazing fashion, is presenting a nontraditional solo piece by David Finnigan about the climate crisis. Part lecture, part storytelling, it weaves personal anecdotal material from the brutal 2019 Australian fire season with historical info from other crisis points in human history. David's presence is approachable and captivating and this piece aims to contextualize the current climate crisis with the past 75,000 years of humanity. It's informative with valuable insights about the climate crisis, but in the end it was too self-reflective to really say something or leave a message that sticks. And to me this was not really theater, but more of a lecture with some narrative devices. Which is fine, but any attempts at making certain moments actually dramatic were not very successful to me. I'd be interested more to see what David’s stamp would look like on a straight-up play. With that, another playbill for my collection.
